scores.critic: Most fragments omit the actual act, subject, motive or requested help, so named participants rarely become distinct people. Explicit causal pointers sometimes assert connections without explaining them. Requests to act against the asker remain unexplained. Closing labels such as protection or resolved do not show what changed. Concrete paid jobs provide clear actions and practical motives, but instant completion hides decisions and consequences. Repeated plots with changed names dominate. Night City detail is concentrated in currency, gangs and a few props. The refusal prompting someone else to help offers the strongest glimpse of lives continuing beyond the protagonist.

Most traces supply event categories without concrete motives, objects, demands, or usable next steps. Requests to act against the asker remain especially difficult to understand. Causal pointers establish asserted connections but often do not explain them; simultaneous or reversed reporting further obscures some chains. A closing label such as resolved, betrayal, or reckoning supplies little payoff without the actual consequence. Completed contracts also conceal methods and findings, particularly surveillance and missing-person inquiries. Repeated structures make participants interchangeable. Eddies, shards, gangs, and local routes support Night City, but many traces could occur anywhere. The modest repair and escort jobs have the clearest practical reasons and proportionate endings. Explicit refusals provide fair stopping points even when little story develops.
